A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LISTA-VM research. Their text, equations, figures, notation table, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite repagination and relocated material.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original synthetic sparse-recovery experiments, and Appendix F reports meta-training results for LISTA, LISTA-CP, and LISTA-VM.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain the work's original sparse-recovery experiments and meta-training results.

M1.justification: Section 6 revises the stated Transformer training objective from final-query errors across instances to errors summed over all N+1 label positions. The LISTA-VM update, Transformer construction, and read-out procedures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation was changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same noiseless synthetic sparse-recovery task, including fixed and varying measurement matrices, restricted and unrestricted support, and different context lengths. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains ISTA, FISTA, LISTA, LISTA-CP, ALISTA, LISTA-VM, Small TF, and GPT-2, including the existing support-selected and meta-trained variants. Appendix F retains the same meta-trained comparisons.

E3.justification: The revised loss in Section 6 changes the reported training supervision from final-query predictions to all N+1 label positions. Data generation, model sizes, iteration counts, and training budgets remain unchanged. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The support-restriction experiment, comparison of three read-out functions, and analysis of meta-trained classical LISTA methods are retained unchanged in Figure 1 and Appendix F. No new ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies experimental seeds, independent-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The point estimates and training traces retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 render identically, and their reported findings are unchanged. These include LISTA-VM-SS error around 0.07 and Appendix F's errors around 0.68 for LISTA-VM versus around 3 for meta-trained LISTA and LISTA-CP.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.2 gains the explicit restriction n in [N0+1, N+1]. Appendix D.1 corrects Lemma 3's off-diagonal bound to use column j of X instead of column i. The main convergence bounds and proof constructions otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: Transformers implement LISTA-VM with linear convergence, accommodate varying measurement matrices and prompt lengths, and exploit sparse-support structure. The introduction and conclusion clarify these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: New Remark 2 attributes linear convergence to curvature information, interpreting the learned matrices as inverse-Hessian approximations that enable second-order-like optimization. This adds a mechanism explanation; the existing generalization interpretations and noiseless-analysis qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 now explicitly identifies ReLU in the experimental Small TF and connects its configuration to the theoretical four-head construction. It also spells out the retained fixed-X and varying-X testing procedure. Hardware, runtimes, and sample counts are unchanged.

R1.justification: The new convergence remark adds Nesterov (2005) and Nemirovskij and Yudin (1983). Section 4.3 newly acknowledges Bai et al. (2024) for a similar embedding. The training-dynamics literature discussion is moved to Appendix A rather than removed.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the motivation, L2O background, and pre-training/inference distinction. The training-dynamics discussion moves to Appendix A, acknowledgments are added, and affiliations and publication headers are updated. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain identical displays, and the notation table retains its design. Matrix displays in Definition 3.1 and Appendix C.1 are compacted into inline expressions, while the table and proofs are repaginated. These are limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision through the explicit range in Theorem 5.2 and the corrected cross-column index in Lemma 3, while clarifying the training/inference distinction and research positioning. The empirical evidence is unchanged. The training-loss rewrite is not explained as either a correction or a rerun, so it does not establish improved experimental quality.
